From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are among the most common but frequently underestimated comorbidities in patients with epilepsy, with major manifestations including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness, restless legs syndrome, and periodic limb movements of sleep. A complex bidirectional interaction exists between epilepsy and sleep disorders: sleep deprivation, disrupted sleep architecture, and sleep-disordered breathing may increase seizure susceptibility, whereas nocturnal seizures, interictal epileptiform discharges, antiseizure medications, and mood comorbidities may further impair sleep continuity and daytime alertness. Although mechanistic links and individual sleep disorders have received increasing attention, a practical outpatient pathway that connects sleep-related complaints with screening, phenotype recognition, objective testing, and subsequent intervention remains insufficiently defined. From a clinical phenotyping perspective, this review proposes a complaint-based framework for the identification, tiered assessment, and integrated management of sleep comorbidities in epilepsy. The framework translates common sleep complaints into major actionable phenotypes, including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements of sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes, while incorporating life-course and syndrome-specific considerations for children and adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults, patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, and older adults with epilepsy. This review organizes dispersed evidence on sleep and epilepsy into a clinically oriented conceptual framework linking complaint-based entry, tiered assessment, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment. The framework is intended to facilitate recognition and structured clinical reasoning, while its feasibility and effects on patient outcomes require prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Sleep duration and anti-müllerian hormone levels in female firefighters.
papers.abstract: To investigate the relationship between anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) levels and sleep duration in female firefighters. We used baseline data collected at time of enrollment into the Women Firefighter Study, part of the Fire Fighter Cancer Cohort Study (FFCCS), including demographic information, reproductive history, and self-reported average off-duty sleep, along with serum AMH concentration. We used linear regression models to estimate the association between off-duty sleep duration (categorized by <7 hours and ≥ 7 hours on average) and log transformed AMH. We adjusted for age (continuous and squared), body mass index (BMI), and oral contraception use. The formula (exp ( β ^ )-1)*100 was used to calculate the percent difference in AMH values. Among 566 participants, those that reported <7 hours of sleep while off-duty had statistically significantly lower AMH levels compared to those who reported ≥ 7 hours of off-duty sleep (-18.0 %, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -32.7, -0.2). Less than 7 hours of off-duty sleep was associated with lower AMH levels. Increasing off-duty sleep is a potential modifiable risk factor to benefit reproductive health in female firefighters.

papers.title: Change in 1-year health outcomes with a smartwatch-based health program in community-dwelling older adults: SWING-Japan study.
papers.abstract: Wearable devices such as smartwatches may be useful tools for managing lifestyles and health among community-dwelling older adults. We aimed to compare 1-year changes in physical, mental, and cognitive functions and health-related awareness between older adults who participated in a smartwatch-based program and those who did not. This nonrandomized controlled study included participants 65 years of age or older from multiple cohort studies. Participants were asked whether they would use a smartwatch in daily life. Older adults who were willing to use a smartwatch received a smartwatch and participated in the smartwatch-based program, which included monthly feedback newsletters and access to a smartphone application, for at least 3 months (smartwatch group). Those who were unwilling to use a smartwatch comprised the comparison group. A 1:1 propensity score matching ratio was implemented. Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate changes in health outcomes between groups over time. Of the 2,273 participants, 1,026 comprised the smartwatch group and 1,247 comprised the comparison group. After propensity score matching for potential confounders, 1,156 participants (578 matched pairs; median age, 76.0 years [interquartile range, 72.0-80.0 years]; 72.4% women) were included in the analyses. Significant time × group interactions were observed for handgrip strength (p = .016) and sleep awareness (p = .011), whereas no significant interactions were observed for gait speed, depressive symptoms, cognitive function, or exercise awareness. Participation in a smartwatch-based program was associated with modestly better maintenance of handgrip strength and modest improvements in sleep awareness among older adults.

papers.title: Comparing wearable and nearable devices for sleep monitoring: A within-subject comparison of wrist-worn wearable and radar-based nearable devices for naturalistic home-based sleep monitoring.
papers.abstract: Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard for sleep assessment but is intrusive and unsuitable for long-term, real-world monitoring. This study compared a wrist-worn wearable device and a radar-based nearable as potential alternatives for naturalistic, home-based sleep monitoring in a working adult population. Thirty-four working adults (mean age 45.3 years) used both devices for up to six weeks, yielding 620 matched sessions and over 500,000 30-second sleep epochs. Agreement between devices was assessed for total sleep time (TST), wake after sleep onset (WASO), and device-derived sleep stage classification using intraclass correlation (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis and kappa statistics. Agreement was excellent for TST (ICC = 0.91), with wearable underestimating sleep duration by a mean of 3.8 minutes (95% limits of agreement: -74 to +67 minutes, a band of approximately 140 minutes). Agreement was low for WASO (ICC = 0.34), with systematic magnitude-dependent discrepancies. Epoch-level analyses showed substantial agreement for 2-state sleep-wake classification (PABAK = 0.78) but only moderate agreement for 4-state classification (Cohen's κ ≈ 0.49), with the wearable classifying more epochs as light sleep, particularly when the nearable identified wake or REM. While the two device classes provide compatible population-level estimates of total sleep duration, agreement for wake detection and algorithmic sleep stage classification was considerably lower. These findings underscore the need for caution against interchangeable use of wearable and nearable devices for individual-level monitoring or research outcomes dependent on wake or sleep stage metrics.

papers.title: Atrial Fibrillation and Subclinical Thyroid Dysfunction: Revisiting an Underrecognized Association - A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Subclinical thyroid disease, defined by abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) with normal thyroid hormone levels, is common and may be an underrecognized contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on how mild thyroid dysfunction influences AF risk and highlights practical implications for clinical management, drawing on mechanistic studies, observational epidemiology, and major guideline recommendations addressing subclinical hyperthyroidism, subclinical hypothyroidism, and cardiac rhythm outcomes. Subclinical hyperthyroidism shows a consistent association with increased AF risk. Proposed mechanisms include thyroid hormone-mediated changes in cardiac electrophysiology, increased adrenergic sensitivity, and atrial structural and electrical remodeling. Current American Thyroid Association and European Thyroid Association guidance supports treating higher-risk patients, particularly those older than 65 years or with cardiovascular comorbidities, when TSH is below 0.1 mIU/L. In contrast, evidence linking subclinical hypothyroidism to AF is weak. Although it has traditionally been associated with bradyarrhythmias, newer studies suggest a possible modest increase in AF risk. Treatment decisions for subclinical hypothyroidism are more nuanced, with the strongest consensus favoring therapy when TSH exceeds 10.0 mIU/L, while lower-level elevations generally require individualized assessment. Overall, subclinical thyroid dysfunction, especially subclinical hyperthyroidism, appears meaningfully related to AF risk, but important evidence gaps remain, including limited large-scale trial data showing that treatment prevents AF. Because subclinical thyroid disease and AF both increase with age, management should be individualized according to age, TSH severity, cardiovascular risk, and comorbidities.

papers.title: A thalamus-centered network model of restless legs syndrome: an integrative hypothesis illustrated by three clinical phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a clinically heterogeneous sensorimotor disorder whose pathophysiology reflects interacting biological mechanisms rather than a single causal pathway. Established influences-including brain iron biology, dopaminergic regulation, glutamatergic and GABAergic balance, adenosinergic inhibition, and abnormal afferent processing-have typically been studied in isolation, leaving their systems-level relationships insufficiently integrated. To motivate a network-based interpretation, we present three illustrative clinical phenotypes: dopamine-agonist augmentation, sensory-predominant RLS with inadequate response to pregabalin, and persistent symptoms despite partial correction of peripheral iron deficiency. These cases highlight how distinct upstream contexts can converge on similar sensory and sleep-physiological endpoints. Human neuroimaging and neurochemical studies provide convergent evidence for thalamic involvement in RLS, including altered thalamic connectivity, differences in thalamic nuclei and network organization, and increased thalamic glutamate/glutamine signal associated with disturbed sleep. Because the thalamus integrates sensory gating, motor modulation, arousal regulation, and sleep-wake stability, it represents a plausible convergence hub for upstream biological influences. We therefore propose a thalamus-centered convergence model in which iron deficiency, dopaminergic instability, glutamatergic hyperresponsiveness, reduced adenosinergic inhibition, altered GABAergic modulation, and abnormal afferent processing interact to increase the susceptibility of thalamo-cortical networks to sensory and arousal instability. The model does not replace established frameworks; instead, it organizes them within a unified, testable network architecture. We outline six falsifiable predictions for multimodal imaging, sleep microstructure, sensory physiology, and treatment-response studies, providing a structured basis for future mechanistic investigation of RLS.

papers.title: Prevalence and Symptom Network of Co-Occurring Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms and Their Associations with Quality of Life Among Chinese Empty-Nest Older Adults.
papers.abstract: The growing number of empty-nest older adults in China has become a critical public health concern. Living apart from adult children may reduce opportunities for daily family interaction and emotional support and increase feelings of loneliness, potentially increasing vulnerability to anxiety and depressive symptoms. The aim of this study was to investigate the prevalence and network structure of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms, and explored their association with quality of life (QoL) among Chinese empty-nest older adults. We included 5110 empty-nest older adults aged 65 and above from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS2018). Anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, and QoL were respectively assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale-7 (GAD-7), the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale-10 (CESD-10), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-brief (WHOQOL-Bref). Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms were defined as concurrent CESD-10 ≥ 10 and GAD-7 ≥ 5. We performed network analyses of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms to identify central and bridge symptoms, and constructed a flow network to examine their associations with QoL. Multivariable linear regression analyses were conducted to assess the associations between symptom-status groups and QoL after adjustment for potential confounders. The prevalence of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms among Chinese empty-nest older adults was 8.67%. Network analysis revealed CESD3 (felt depressed), GAD4 (trouble relaxing) and GAD2 (uncontrollable worry) exhibited relatively high expected influence (EI) values within the anxiety and depressive symptom network. Concurrently, GAD1 (nervousness), GAD4 (trouble relaxing), CESD1 (bothered by things), and CESD6 (felt fearful) were identified as potential bridge symptoms between anxiety and depressive symptom communities. Moreover, CESD10 (sleep disturbances) showed a relatively strong negative association with quality of life (QoL). After adjustment for potential confounders, all three symptom groups had significantly lower QoL scores than the control group (depression-only: β = -0.96; anxiety-only: β = -0.33; co-occurring symptoms: β = -1.28; all p ≤ 0.001). Pairwise comparisons further showed that the co-occurring symptoms group had lower QoL scores than both the depression-only group (mean difference = -0.32, p < 0.001) and the anxiety-only group (mean difference = -0.95, p < 0.001). Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms are relatively common among Chinese empty-nest older adults and are significantly associated with poorer quality of life. It is important to pay attention to both central and bridge symptoms when assessing mental health in this population. Interventions aimed at addressing sleep disturbances among empty-nest older adults may be beneficial for supporting their mental health and improving their quality of life.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a prodromal stage of Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aimed to investigate whether gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) show consistent alterations in iRBD and PD with RBD patients. We enrolled 29 iRBD, 24 PD with RBD, 17 PD without RBD, and 18 normal controls (NC). Fecal microbiota composition was analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing, and SCFA concentrations via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Clinical symptoms were assessed using motor and non-motor scales, and Spearman correlation analysis was performed to explore interrelationships. Microbiota analysis revealed that, compared with NC, Bifidobacterium, Blautia_A, and Azospira_A were significantly enriched, whereas Agathobaculum, Clostridium_Q, Faecalibaculum, Photobacterium, Copromonas, UBA3402, Acetobacter, and Sutterella were reduced in both iRBD and PD with RBD groups. SCFA analysis showed significantly decreased fecal butyric acid and propionic acid levels in both groups versus NC. Correlation analysis demonstrated that in the iRBD group, Bifidobacterium positively correlated with RBD disease duration; butyric acid negatively correlated with NMSS and RBD-HK; propionic acid negatively correlated with NMSS, RBD-HK, and SCOPA-AUT. In the PD with RBD group, Bifidobacterium negatively correlated with SCOPA-AUT and positively with HAMD-17; butyric acid positively correlated with MDS-UPDRS III. iRBD and PD with RBD share similar gut dysbiosis and SCFA abnormalities. Elevated Bifidobacterium and decreased butyric acid and propionic acid are candidate markers for iRBD risk stratification, but correlation does not imply predictive ability. Their value in predicting progression to PD requires validation in longitudinal iRBD cohorts.
keywords: rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder

papers.title: Aberrant Interregional Brain Connectivity During Different Memory Processes in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Reduced working memory is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Analyzing local field potentials (LFPs) across neural networks provides crucial insights into the mechanisms underlying these cognitive deficits. Standard LFP studies often rely on spontaneous exploration, while we designed a novel Y-maze paradigm with aversive voltage feedback. This paradigm enable precise time-locked temporal subdivision of trials (first choice vs. second choice, correct vs. incorrect decisionst) to compare memory-related electrophysiology between AD and normal mice. Our analysis reveals four key findings: (1) LFP exhibit task-specific lateralization, suggesting the right hemisphere is prominently engaged during this specific spatial navigation context; (2) correct behavioral outcomes correlate with pre-decision neural states, highlighting distinct network encoding mechanisms compared to error processing; (3) causal connectivity suggests a disrupted functional balance between the cingulate gyrus and hippocampus in AD mice, it may reflect early network compensation; (4) AD mice display widespread oscillatory and directional connectivity disruptions during memory process, which strongly correlate with spatial memory failures. These findings characterize AD memory impairment as a dynamic network disconnectivity syndrome and highlight cingulate gyrus-hippocampal interactions as potential biomarkers to improve memory dysfunction in AD.

papers.title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
papers.abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2). Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation. Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.

papers.title: Circadian orchestration of the cutaneous microenvironment and chronotherapeutic strategies in inflammatory skin diseases.
papers.abstract: The clinical course of inflammatory skin diseases-encompassing atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and chronic spontaneous urticaria-frequently exhibits pronounced symptomatic rhythmicity, most classically manifested as the nocturnal exacerbation of pruritus. Although previous studies have progressively elucidated the circadian mechanisms governing both the epidermal barrier and local immunity that drive lesion evolution, contemporary clinical regimens for most targeted therapeutics and biologics have yet to incorporate administration timing as a key variable for optimizing efficacy. This review systematically delineates the dynamic interactive network between skin barrier function and the immune microenvironment under the regulation of the endogenous circadian clock. Building upon this mechanistic foundation, we examine how the timing of each major drug class-topical agents, conventional systemic drugs, oral small molecules and macromolecular biologics-could be aligned with the circadian peaks of the mediators they target, and we distinguish the components of this framework that are supported by clinical data from those that remain hypotheses. Ultimately, by conceptualizing chronotherapeutic strategies for precise intervention in local microenvironmental rhythms, this article aims to provide a testable framework for future chronotherapeutic research in inflammatory skin diseases.

papers.title: Glymphatic dysfunction and amyloid-β clearance in Alzheimer's disease: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system supports cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid (CSF-ISF) exchange and extracellular solute transport, and its dysfunction may contribute to amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation in Alzheimer's disease (AD). This narrative review examines mechanisms linking impaired brain fluid transport to Aβ retention, focusing on altered perivascular aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization, vascular and paravascular remodeling, impaired cerebrovascular dynamics, astrocyte dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and sleep and circadian disturbances. It also evaluates preclinical evidence for Chinese herbal interventions. Preclinical studies have reported changes in CSF tracer influx or distribution, parenchymal solute efflux, meningeal lymphatic tracer transport, AQP4 localization, and lymphatic vessel morphology, often accompanied by reduced Aβ burden and improved cognitive performance. Other studies primarily report changes in cellular Aβ handling, inflammation, or sleep and therefore provide only indirect support for glymphatic involvement. Glymphatic exchange, intramural periarterial drainage, and meningeal lymphatic outflow are anatomically distinct processes with different experimental readouts; reduced tissue Aβ alone does not establish enhanced clearance. Major limitations include heterogeneity in experimental models and tracer methods, limited pathway-specific causal validation, and a lack of clinical evidence directly supporting these mechanisms of action. Dynamic transport measurements, pathway-specific perturbations, and standardized formulations are needed to determine whether enhancement of brain fluid and solute clearance represents a clinically translatable mechanism of Chinese herbal interventions in AD.

papers.title: New-onset depersonalization-derealization syndrome following semaglutide therapy.
papers.abstract: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, acts on central neuropsychiatric pathways beyond its metabolic effects, yet dissociative adverse effects have rarely been reported. We describe a 42-year-old woman with no psychiatric history who developed recurrent, distressing episodes of depersonalization and derealization approximately 7 days after her second 0.5 mg weekly dose of semaglutide prescribed for obesity. The episodes progressed from once daily to 3 to 4 times daily over 10 days, with insight and reality testing preserved throughout. Metabolic, neurological, toxicological, and psychiatric evaluations, including brain imaging, electroencephalography, and laboratory studies, excluded alternative causes. She fulfilled the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition criteria for depersonalization-derealization disorder, and the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score of 6 indicated a probable causal relationship. Semaglutide was discontinued without psychotropic medication, and symptoms resolved completely within 4 weeks, with sustained remission at 3 months. This case suggests that depersonalization-derealization is an underrecognized, reversible neuropsychiatric adverse effect of semaglutide and underscores the need for clinician awareness and patient counseling during therapy.

papers.title: Psychological factors in tumor immunity: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy. However, durable responses remain limited to a subset of patients. Accumulating evidence suggests that psychological factors, particularly chronic psychological stress (CPS), depression, and anxiety, may influence responses to immunotherapy. This review synthesizes recent evidence concerning three major pathways: the sympathetic nervous system-norepinephrine-beta-adrenergic receptor (SNS-NE-β-AR) axis, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal-glucocorticoid (HPA-GC) axis, and vagus nerve-acetylcholine (VN-ACh) signaling. We summarize how catecholamines, glucocorticoids, and cholinergic mediators affect antitumor immunity. These mediators can promote effector T-cell dysfunction, recruit immunosuppressive myeloid cells, alter macrophage polarization, and regulate immune-checkpoint expression. They are also involved in tumor innervation and metabolic reprogramming. We further evaluate both pharmacological and nonpharmacological strategies targeting these pathways. Pharmacological approaches include β-blockers, inhibitors of glucocorticoid synthesis or metabolism, glucocorticoid-receptor antagonists, and cholinergic-receptor blockers. Nonpharmacological strategies include cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based stress reduction, environmental enrichment, and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation. Although preclinical studies and retrospective clinical analyses provide a rationale for targeting these pathways, the available evidence is heterogeneous and requires confirmation in adequately powered prospective trials. Integrating psychological assessment with neuroendocrine and immune biomarkers may support risk stratification and the development of individualized combination strategies.

papers.title: Suspected Functional Adrenal Insufficiency and Unmasking of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Case for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Restraint.
papers.abstract: A man in his 30s presented with progressive weight loss, fatigue, anorexia, and low mood that developed over several weeks following international migration and transition to night shift work, the changes that disrupted his sleep-wake cycle and circadian rhythm. A low 8 am cortisol level (2.9 mcg/dL) with a borderline low ACTH concentration (7.4 pg/mL), negative anti-adrenal antibodies, normal electrolytes, and unremarkable adrenal imaging, suggestive of secondary adrenal insufficiency. Given his hemodynamic stability, empirical glucocorticoid therapy was deliberately deferred in favor of cessation of night shift work, sleep restoration, and nutritional rehabilitation, which resulted in complete clinical and biochemical resolution within weeks. At six months follow-up, a rising thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level, strongly positive thyroid peroxidase antibodies, and a heterogeneous thyroid on ultrasound revealed previously unrecognized Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a finding consistent with cortisol inhibitory effect on TSH secretion during adrenal suppression. This case illustrates that circadian rhythm disruption from night shift work and migration can produce a reversible functional form of secondary adrenal insufficiency that may resolve without glucocorticoid replacement. It underscores the value of detailed occupational and sleep history in patients presenting with unexplained constitutional symptoms and highlights how cortisol-TSH interactions can transiently mask the co-existing autoimmune thyroid disease. Clinicians should consider a period of clinical reassessment before treating hemodynamically stable patients with long-term glucocorticoid therapy and should reassess thyroid function once adrenal function normalizes.
papers.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Endocrinology and diabetes

papers.title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Migraine patients show choroid plexus (CP) changes, impairing the blood-CSF barrier. The CP regulates circadian rhythms, but links between CP circadian genes and migraine are unexplored. This study examined changes in the CP circadian gene transcriptome in a chronic migraine rat model compared with controls to identify migraine-related pathways. Chronic migraine model: Sprague-Dawley rats (3 females, 3 males) received nitroglycerin (NTG) every other day for 9 days; controls (3 females, 3 males) got saline. CP from the 4th ventricle was collected 2 hours after the final injection for RNA-seq. Migraine Behavior: Von Frey hair tests on days 1, 5, and 9, pre- and 2 hours post-NTG/saline injection, assessed basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds. RNA-seq & Analysis: Differentially expressed genes (p < 0.05, fold change > 1) were identified. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed to assess changes in circadian gene expression. The NTG group showed reduced basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds on days 1, 5, and 9. Females had a greater number of upregulated genes (MT2A, SLC7A11); males had upregulated ZBTB16 and S100A8. SLC7A11, SCG2, and GRIA1 showed inverse regulation (up in females, down in males). Circadian gene expression altered: 10 genes upregulated (e.g., SERPINE1, MAPK9, ATF4), 13 downregulated (e.g., PER2, DBP, EZH2). Sex-specific differences: females (FBXL12, GPR157), males (NKX2-1, ATF4, CLOCK). GO/KEGG analyses revealed significant enrichment of circadian rhythm-related pathways, insulin resistance, and inflammatory response processes, with sex-specific differences: females showed enrichment in HIF-1 signaling and hemoglobin-related pathways, while males exhibited enrichment in arachidonic acid and leukotriene production. CP transcriptomics in the rat migraine model revealed sex-specific gene regulation, with females upregulating antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) and males upregulating inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8), alongside circadian disruption (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated). Pathway analyses indicate enriched circadian rhythms, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory processes (males), lipid metabolism (PPARα), and heme signaling, highlighting sex-specific and circadian targets for migraine therapy.
papers.journal: Journal of central nervous system disease

papers.title: Standardized botanical blend for vasomotor and nonvasomotor menopause symptoms: A decentralized open label trial.
papers.abstract: To characterize changes in vasomotor, sleep, musculoskeletal, and psychological symptoms of menopause during treatment with a standardized botanical blend (SBB). This decentralized open label trial of SBB was performed in the United States between May and December 2024. The SBB contains curcumin, green tea extract, and phycocyanin, and reduces hypothalamic neurokinin B signaling in animal models. Perimenopausal or postmenopausal women experiencing ≥5 moderate-to-severe hot flashes (HF) daily received SBB for 12 weeks. Vasomotor symptoms were assessed using daily HF diaries and the Hot Flash Related Daily Interference Scale (HFRDIS). Sleep was evaluated using the PROMIS Sleep Disturbance (PROMIS-SD) short form (SF-8b). Psychological symptoms and quality of life were assessed with the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), Greene Climacteric Scale (GCS), and MENQOL. Musculoskeletal symptoms were captured with an exploratory joint and muscle pain questionnaire. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mixed-model repeated measures and dichotomized responder rates were evaluated using categorical tests. 134 participants completed the study. With SBB supplementation, mean within-subject moderate to severe HF frequency decreased by -2.7 per day (58.5% reduction) at week 4 and -3.3 per day (71.6% reduction) at week 12 (p <0.001). Sleep disturbance improved significantly, with a reduction in PROMIS-SD T-score of -7.2 (95% CI: [-8.7, -5.8]) at week 4 and -9.0 [-10.7, -7.2] at week 12 (p <0.001). Musculoskeletal pain ratings declined by 38.6% and 43.4% at weeks 4 and 12, respectively (p <0.001). Psychological symptoms scales also showed commensurate improvement. Responder rates significantly improved from baseline in all domains. Improvements met or exceeded the accepted threshold for minimal clinical important difference. SBB supplementation was associated with clinically significant improvements across vasomotor and nonvasomotor symptom domains.

papers.title: ASTRO study: acupuncture sets of trial reported core outcomes for women's health across the lifespan.
papers.abstract: Clinical trials of acupuncture are difficult to meaningfully aggregate due to small sample sizes and reductionist, heterogeneous outcome measures. To improve the quality of evidence, standardised reporting of minimum data that reflects whole-person health, essential to East Asian Medicine (EAM), is needed. The Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative offers a methodology for developing core outcome sets (COS) through collaborative group consensus, including consumers. This study presents the 'Acupuncture Sets of Trial Reported Outcomes' (ASTRO) for women's health. Using domains of pain, sleep, mood/cognition and safety, the ASTRO framework captures EAM complexity as well as standardising reporting outcomes. To develop a COS for acupuncture trials in women's health, reflecting whole-person health outcomes across the lifespan. We used a COMET-informed three-stage consensus process involving practitioners, researchers, patients and policymakers to develop a COS for reporting minimum data for acupuncture trials in women's health. This process involved a systematic review, roundtable discussion, two-round Delphi survey and a consensus meeting. We examined the conditions of menstrual health, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, fertility, pregnancy and menopause to develop an outcome set for safety, feasibility and EAM specific outcomes. From 320 studies, 579 outcomes were identified for the survey items and 319 respondents participated in two Delphi survey rounds. The attrition rate was 52% between surveys and respondents were mainly from English-speaking countries. A final COS of 12 outcomes was agreed on:Safety (n=2): serious adverse events and minor adverse events.EAM (n=8): primary and secondary patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), patient experience/satisfaction, EAM diagnostic indices (eg, tongue and pulse), demographics and changes in pain, sleep and mood/cognition.Feasibility (n=2): acceptability and cost. The ASTRO Women's Health COS enables consistent, whole-person outcome reporting to improve the quality and comparability of acupuncture research.

papers.title: Characteristics and significance of gut microbiota alterations in patients with acute myocardial infarction and their association with the occurrence of heart failure.
papers.abstract: In the context of real-world clinical practice, this study aimed to systematically investigate the characteristics of gut microecological alterations in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), elucidate their potential clinical significance, and further analyze the association between gut microbiota imbalance and the short-term occurrence of heart failure (HF) in AMI patients, as well as the related influencing factors. This study adopted a single-center retrospective case-control design. A total of 143 AMI patients who received standardized diagnosis and treatment in our hospital between April 2023 and June 2025 were enrolled as the disease group, while 120 healthy volunteers undergoing physical examination during the same period were selected as the control group. Selected cultivable gut microbial groups in both groups were quantitatively assessed using culture-based methods. All AMI patients were followed up for 30 days and were divided into group A (HF occurred, n=44) and group B (HF did not occur, n=99) according to whether HF events occurred during the follow-up period. Differences in gut microbiota composition and cardiac function-related indicators, including N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), were compared between the two groups. Correlation analysis and multivariable logistic regression models were applied to explore the relationships between the selected gut microbial indicators and cardiac function indicators and to identify factors independently associated with HF occurrence in AMI patients. Compared with the control group, the disease group showed a significant increase in the number of conditional pathogenic bacteria and aerobic bacteria in the gut, with markedly higher levels of Enterobacter, Enterococcus, Clostridium, fungi, and total aerobic bacteria (P<0.05). In contrast, beneficial bacteria were significantly reduced, as evidenced by decreased levels of Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, and total anaerobic bacteria (P<0.05). Further subgroup analysis revealed that, compared with group B, group A had significantly lower abundances of beneficial bacteria (Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, and total anaerobic bacteria), while the numbers of Enterobacter, Enterococcus, and total aerobic bacteria were markedly increased (P<0.05). Meanwhile, LVEF levels were significantly lower and NT-proBNP levels were significantly higher in group A than in group B (P<0.05). Correlation analysis showed that the numbers of Enterobacter, Enterococcus, and total aerobic bacteria were significantly positively correlated with NT-proBNP levels and negatively correlated with LVEF (P<0.05). Conversely, the numbers of Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, and total anaerobic bacteria were negatively correlated with NT-proBNP and positively correlated with LVEF (P<0.05). Multivariate regression analysis further confirmed that Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, total anaerobic bacteria, LVEF, Enterobacter, Enterococcus, total aerobic bacteria, and NT-proBNP were all independent influencing factors for the occurrence of HF in AMI patients. AMI patients exhibit a certain degree of alteration in gut microbiota structure, mainly characterized by a reduction in the abundance of some beneficial bacteria and a relative increase in conditional pathogenic bacteria. These gut microecological changes are associated with cardiac function indicators and the short-term occurrence of HF, suggesting that gut microbiota imbalance may have a potential link with adverse cardiac functional outcomes after AMI. However, given that this study was a single-center retrospective investigation, the findings still require further validation in larger, multicenter, and prospective studies.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and variable intellectual and behavioral abnormalities (NEDHIB) is a rare autosomal-dominant condition caused by pathogenic POLR2A variants. It typically presents in infancy with hypotonia, developmental delay, and multisystem manifestations. Fewer than 40 patients have been reported worldwide, suggesting frequent misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. To our knowledge, neurodevelopmental regression has not been documented in confirmed NEDHIB cases, and no standardized therapeutic regimens are established for clinical management. The patient presented with neonatal hypotonia and developmental delay. At 2 years and 4 months, she developed sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding and limb tremors that were initially suspected to represent epileptic seizures. By 3 years of age, she exhibited marked neurodevelopmental regression: loss of the ability to walk and sit independently, together with deterioration of language function. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated background slowing accompanied by epileptiform discharges. Whole-exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous POLR2A variant c.3379C > T (p. L1127F), which confirmed the diagnosis of NEDHIB. Long-term rehabilitation training yielded only modest clinical benefits. After initiation of the dopamine agent levodopa-benserazide hydrochloride, marked improvements in motor and cognitive performance were observed, accompanied by the complete resolution of nodding episodes. With dose titration during follow-up, her clinical status remained stable without symptom relapse. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum associated with POLR2A-related NEDHIB and suggests that neurodevelopmental regression may occur within the phenotypic spectrum of this disorder. Our findings also highlight the potential benefit of low-dose dopamine therapy, offering novel insights into the clinical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic management of NEDHIB.

papers.title: Effect of a Nurse-Led Sleep Hygiene and Progressive Muscle Relaxation Intervention on Sleep Quality Among Obese Pregnant Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are a common challenge among obese pregnant women and are associated with adverse maternal outcomes. Evidence-based nonpharmacological interventions may improve sleep quality; however, robust evidence remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a nurse-led sleep hygiene education and progressive muscle relaxation intervention on sleep quality among obese pregnant women. A randomized controlled trial was conducted on 100 obese pregnant women with sleep disturbance. Women were randomly assigned to either a control group (with standard antenatal care) or a study group (with structured progressive muscle relaxation and sleep hygiene). The study was conducted at the antenatal clinics of Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital, Cairo University Hospitals. Data were collected using the Structured Interview Schedule, Global Sleep Assessment Questionnaire (GSAQ), Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and self-Reported Intervention Adherence Checklist. There were no statistically significant differences between the study and control groups in terms of demographic and obstetric data (p > 0.05). The study group demonstrated significant improvements in sleep outcomes compared with the control group receiving routine antenatal care. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significant time-by-group interactions for sleep disorders (F = 73.404, p < 0.001), sleep quality (F = 59.643, p < 0.001), and sleep hygiene (F = 97.128, p < 0.001). The study group demonstrated statistically significant improvements in all components of sleep quality; mean scores decreased consistently from preintervention to postintervention across all PSQI components, indicating marked improvements in overall sleep quality. The greatest reductions were observed in subjective sleep quality (2.30 ± 0.763 vs. 0.68 ± 0.844), sleep efficiency (2.14 ± 0.808 vs. 0.56 ± 0.733), sleep disturbance (2.08 ± 0.528 vs. 0.70 ± 0.839), and the use of sleep medication (2.42 ± 0.859 vs. 1.14 ± 0.969). The intervention demonstrated large effect sizes for sleep disorders (partial η 2 = 0.428), sleep quality (partial η 2 = 0.378), and sleep hygiene (partial η 2 = 0.498), indicating substantial improvements following the intervention. The study group had a 50% lower risk of low sleep quality (RR = 0.50; ARR = 0.46) in comparison with the women of the control group. The nurse-led sleep hygiene education and progressive muscle relaxation intervention improved sleep quality, sleep disorder symptoms, and sleep hygiene practices among obese pregnant women compared with routine antenatal care. This combined nonpharmacological intervention may be a useful addition to antenatal nursing care, although further research using objective sleep assessments and longer follow-up is recommended. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06890910.
authors: Ebtesam Abdel Nabi Abdel Hamid Behery

papers.title: Editorial: Advances in perceptual decision making and brain oscillations.
Caffeine as a context-dependent metabolic, perceptual, and recovery modulator in exercise: implications for substrate utilization, performance, and individual responsiveness.
papers.abstract: Caffeine is a widely studied ergogenic aid in sport and exercise science, yet its effects on exercise metabolism, performance, and recovery remain context dependent. Although caffeine is commonly used to enhance alertness, reduce perceived exertion, and improve exercise capacity, its effects vary with dose, ingestion timing, delivery form, exercise modality, habitual caffeine intake, training status, sex-related factors, genotype, and sleep vulnerability. This narrative review provides an evidence-calibrated synthesis of caffeine's central, metabolic, perceptual, performance-related, and recovery-related effects, emphasizing substrate utilization and individual responsiveness. It distinguishes relatively well-supported mechanisms from conditional or inconsistent effects, examines major sources of heterogeneity across studies, and evaluates acute ergogenic benefits alongside potential recovery costs. Evidence indicates that caffeine's most consistent mechanisms involve adenosine receptor antagonism, increased central nervous system activation, and reduced perception of effort or fatigue. Peripheral and metabolic mechanisms, including catecholamine-mediated substrate mobilization, changes in fat oxidation, calcium handling, and glycogen-related responses, are biologically plausible but appear more conditional and protocol dependent. Importantly, caffeine-induced increases in fat oxidation should not be interpreted as direct evidence of glycogen sparing or performance enhancement, because their practical relevance depends on exercise intensity, duration, carbohydrate availability, and the performance outcome assessed. Caffeine shows the strongest ergogenic evidence in endurance exercise, while effects on strength, power, repeated sprint ability, and sport-specific skills are smaller and more variable. Recovery-related applications require particular caution: caffeine may support perceived readiness or selected glycogen-related outcomes when combined with carbohydrate in short-turnaround contexts, but late-day ingestion may impair sleep and thereby compromise broader recovery. Overall, caffeine should be understood as a context-dependent metabolic and perceptual modulator rather than a universally ergogenic supplement. Applied use should prioritize the lowest effective dose, individualized timing, sport-specific trialling, adverse-effect monitoring, and careful consideration of recovery costs. Future research should integrate metabolic markers, performance outcomes, sleep, and individual moderators within ecologically valid sport protocols to clarify when caffeine is beneficial, neutral, or potentially counterproductive.

papers.title: Crosstalk mechanisms, clinical correlations and therapeutic implications linking OSA with HFpEF progression.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is closely associated with and represents a potential biological contributor to the onset and progression of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Although abundant studies have clarified the associations of OSA with cardiovascular diseases including hypertension, coronary artery disease, arrhythmia and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), the exact pathophysiological mechanisms underlying OSA-related HFpEF remain poorly elucidated, and relevant systematic reviews are still scarce. This review summarizes the pathophysiological links and clinical correlations between OSA and HFpEF. Beyond classical mechanisms such as intrathoracic pressure swings and sympathetic overactivation, we highlight the pivotal roles of systemic inflammation, obesity, vascular injury and metabolic dysfunction in disease progression. We further elaborate how these interactive pathological pathways shape a clinically identifiable OSA-HFpEF phenotype, and summarize phenotype-based diagnostic strategies. Moreover, we discuss therapeutic implications for targeted management for patients with isolated OSA and comorbid OSA-HFpEF. Finally, we outline existing limitations and future research perspectives in the mechanistic exploration, diagnosis and management of OSA-HFpEF comorbidity.
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

papers.title: Leisure-time sedentary behavior and psychosocial distress among intermediate-school adolescents in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Leisure-time sedentary behavior is strongly linked to poorer psychosocial wellbeing among adolescents. In Saudi Arabia, however, where adolescents have among the highest reported levels of screen-based media use, this association is notably under-researched. To address this gap in the literature, the current study investigated the association between leisure-time sedentary behavior and psychosocial wellbeing using the metrics of loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance among Saudi intermediate-school adolescents. Adopting a cross-sectional research design, a stratified multi-stage sample of Saudi adolescents (N = 5,895; grades 7-9) was recruited from 40 public intermediate schools across five Saudi cities in 2019 using a modified Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS). Leisure-time sedentary behavior (a single self-report sitting/screen-time item) was dichotomized at ≥3 h/day ("high"). Loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance were assessed individually and as a composite distress score (two items, 0-3 each, summed; distress = score ≥3). Logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, nationality, city, physical activity, and sleep duration, estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR), with standard errors clustered by school (N = 40) to account for students being sampled within, rather than independently of, schools. Just over half (52.2%) reported high sedentary behavior (≥3 h/day), which was significantly associated with composite psychological distress (aOR 1.55, 95% CI 1.33-1.80), loneliness (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.19-1.58), and anxiety-related sleep disturbance (aOR 1.64, 95% CI 1.38-1.94); crude and adjusted estimates were similar. An exploratory dose-response analysis showed a pattern visually consistent with a threshold, with odds rising significantly only beyond 6-7 h/day; the significant ≥3 h/day association was likely driven by this highest-exposure subgroup. Distress similarly increased with age from 14 onwards, and girls were approximately twice as likely to report distress as boys (aOR 2.09). High leisure-time sedentary behavior was independently associated with loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance among the sampled Saudi intermediate-school adolescents, particularly at the highest exposure levels. As the design was cross-sectional, these findings describe an association, not causation; longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to establish direction and to test whether reducing sedentary behavior improves psychosocial outcomes in this population.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is important for diagnosing and managing sleep disorders. However, artificial intelligence-based models still struggle with explainability, sequence plausibility, and personalization across subjects. We propose LogicSleep, a neurosymbolic framework that integrates transition rules with deep learning models for explainable, physiologically valid, and subject-adaptive sleep staging. LogicSleep extracts multi-level evidence from raw polysomnography via a CNN-graph U-Net backbone, providing explainable patterns beyond classification. Sequence plausibility is enforced by combining Conditional Random Fields with Deep Learning with Differentiable Logics (DL2) rules, which discourage implausible transitions, promote physiologically valid ones, and regularize dwell times; the same rules also guide subject-specific test-time adaptation via entropy minimization. Across different datasets (i.e., ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 datasets), under both within- and cross-dataset settings, LogicSleep consistently outperforms strong baselines and improves sequence-level metrics. Ablations confirm complementary contributions of each component. LogicSleep advances sleep staging toward physiologically plausible, personalized, and explainable predictions.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset for the study of cybersickness under stress and mental workload during immersive VR driving.
papers.abstract: Cybersickness is a common issue in immersive virtual reality (VR), causing symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, and eye strain. In demanding VR training scenarios, stress and mental workload may influence cybersickness severity. However, further research requires datasets that capture these factors alongside subjective and objective measures. This paper presents a multimodal dataset collected during a VR driving simulation to investigate cybersickness in relation to stress and mental workload. Sixty participants completed a phase-based driving task in immersive VR. All participants performed three initial driving phases with progressively increasing difficulty, followed by a condition-specific final phase designed to elicit mental workload, stress, or a combination of both (20 participants per condition). Self-report questionnaires assessing cybersickness, mental workload, and stress-related symptoms were administered at multiple time points during the experiment. Physiological and behavioral data were continuously recorded using an instrumented VR headset and wearable sensors, including electroencephalography (EEG), cardiovascular signals, respiration, and head movement. Representative analyses of subjective and objective measures were conducted to validate the dataset. The analyses demonstrate changes in cybersickness symptoms across driving phases and experimental conditions, illustrating the potential of the collected data to examine cybersickness alongside stress and mental workload. This multimodal dataset provides a resource for neuroergonomics research on cybersickness in immersive VR driving scenarios. By integrating self-reported symptoms with physiological and behavioral measurements, it supports future investigations into the relationships between cybersickness, stress, and mental workload, as well as the development of approaches for monitoring and mitigating cybersickness in demanding VR applications.

papers.title: Exploratory evaluation of electroencephalogram-derived features for classification of mild cognitive impairment in two independent datasets.
papers.abstract: A proper diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is one of the important challenges in the early detection of dementia. For the classification of MCI patients and healthy controls, some electroencephalogram (EEG)-derived indices were calculated and compared. Some studies have been conducted on the high accuracy classification of MCI patients and healthy controls, but classification may depend on the dataset and recording conditions. In this study, we evaluated EEG-derived indices in the Japanese and the Iranian EEG datasets and examined their classification performance under within-dataset and cross-dataset validation. This classifier had common features but was learned for each dataset. The Japanese dataset consisted of 7 MCI patients and 10 healthy controls. The Iranian dataset consisted of 29 MCI patients and 32 healthy controls. The common 16 EEG data were separated into 5 frequency bands. Power spectrum and SL values by Synchronization Likelihood were calculated as features for classification. These standardized and exponentially transformed indices were also used as features. Furthermore, graph metrics were calculated based on SL values before or after standardization and exponential transformation. Features used for classification were selected from these indices. The high classification accuracies were obtained from the classifier using a 34-dimensional feature subset selected from standardized and exponentially transformed EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band. Accuracies of this classifier were 88.24% in the Japanese dataset and 86.89% in the Iranian dataset. To evaluate classification accuracy while minimizing information leakage and optimistic bias, nested leave-one-out cross-validation was performed. Accuracies were 88.24% in the Japanese dataset and 83.61% in the Iranian dataset using exponentially transformed EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band. To evaluate whether the classifier can generalize to independent datasets obtained under different recording conditions, exploratory bidirectional cross-dataset evaluation was performed. Accuracies were 40.98% (Training data: the Japanese dataset, Test data: the Iranian dataset) and 58.82% (Training data: the Iranian dataset, Test data: the Japanese dataset). These findings suggested that resting-state EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band may contain information useful for classification of MCI patients and healthy controls. However, they suggested that classifier based on these indices may partly reflect dataset-specific characteristics.

papers.title: Sleep symptoms, reproductive hormones, and treatment trajectories across the menopausal transition: analyses of two observational cohorts.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is common during the menopausal transition, but whether menopausal context is associated with the pace of improvement during insomnia treatment is unclear. We first examined associations of menopausal stage and reproductive-hormone variation with sleep symptoms in a community cohort, and then sleep-quality trajectories during routine insomnia treatment across estimated menopausal proxy groups in a clinical cohort. Two observational cohorts were analysed separately. The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation (SWAN) included 3,280 women and 22,925 person-visits; mixed-effects and generalized-estimating-equation models examined stage-related symptom burden, annual persistence, and within- versus between-woman hormone associations. The clinical cohort comprised 431 women receiving insomnia treatment (a hospital-affiliated digital sleep programme delivering cognitive-behavioural and relaxation content, pharmacotherapy, or both) in three estimated hormone-plus-age proxy groups (99 regular-cycling, 89 perimenopausal, 243 postmenopausal), with 2,522 Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) assessments over 12 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated average monthly PSQI change (points/month) by group; logistic and Cox models estimated response, remission, and time to first observed response. In SWAN, sleep-symptom burden increased across the menopausal transition (ordinal trend +0.23 points per stage on the 3-15 score, p < 0.001); late perimenopause had the largest adjusted burden difference relative to premenopause (β = 0.788, p < 0.001). Persistence odds were higher in early perimenopause (OR = 1.281, p = 0.002) and natural postmenopause (OR = 1.389, p = 0.003). Higher log-transformed follicle-stimulating hormone (β = 0.221) and lower log-estradiol (β = -0.144), relative to each woman's own mean, were associated with greater burden (both p < 0.001); between-woman hormone terms were not significant. In the clinical cohort, PSQI scores improved in all proxy groups (estimated slopes -0.65, -0.45, and -0.67 points/month in the regular-cycling, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal groups, respectively). The perimenopause-versus-regular slope contrast was +0.198 points/month (95% CI -0.060 to 0.455, p = 0.133; false-discovery-rate q = 0.532), and no perimenopause-focused contrast for response, remission, or time to response was statistically significant. Menopausal stage and within-woman reproductive-hormone variation were associated with sleep-symptom burden in SWAN. During routine insomnia treatment, sleep quality improved in all estimated menopausal proxy groups, and average improvement trajectories did not differ significantly between groups. Prospective studies with menstrual-history-based staging and standardised treatment are needed.

papers.title: Effectiveness and safety of different administration routes of medical cannabis or cannabinoids for chronic pain in adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis with GRADE assessment.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain lasting more than 3 months affects more than one billion people globally, ranking as the third most prevalent health burden, after cardiovascular diseases and malignancies. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of medical cannabis or cannabinoids for chronic pain in adults, with prespecified subgroup analyses stratified by pain etiology and administration route to support precision pain management. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from each database's inception to 15 March 2025. The certainty of evidence was assessed with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. The focused outcomes were pain relief, sleep quality, physical and emotional functioning, anxiety, depression, and adverse events. Twenty-eight studies were involved. Compared to placebo, palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) (SMD = -0.82, 95% CI:-1.36 to -0.29; very low) and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) (SMD = -0.41, 95% CI:-0.74 to -0.07; low) provided pain relief, and a THC/cannabidiol (CBD) combination significantly improved sleep quality (SMD = -0.43, 95% CI:-0.62 to -0.24; moderate). Regarding safety outcomes, compared to placebo, THC (RR = 3.55, 95% CI: 2.21 to 5.68; low) and THC/CBD (RR = 2.70, 95% CI: 1.60 to 4.53; high) had a relatively high rate of dizziness, and THC (RR = 2.72, 95% CI: 1.76 to 4.22; low) and THC/CBD (RR = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.74 to 4.90; high) had a significant risk of somnolence. THC/CBD elevated nausea risk (RR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.26 to 2.60; high), while THC increased dry mouth incidence (RR = 3.14, 95% CI: 1.75 to 5.63; moderate). Additionally, compared with placebo for pain relief, CBD demonstrated the greatest effectiveness for cancer-related pain (SMD = -1.62, 95% CI:-2.03 to -1.21), whereas PEA showed optimal effectiveness in non-cancer-related pain (SMD = -0.82, 95% CI:-1.31 to -0.33). This study suggested that medical cannabis or cannabinoids might have certain efficacy for adult chronic pain. PEA and THC provided pain relief, while the THC/CBD combination showed a potential benefit for sleep quality improvement. THC was associated with increased risks of dizziness, somnolence, and dry mouth, and THC/CBD was associated with dizziness, somnolence, and nausea. Subgroup analyses suggested that treatment response might vary by pain etiology and administration route. Given that the evidence certainty is mainly low to very low, the research conclusion still requires a large sample and high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to be verified. https://osf.io/h56g9, Unique Identifier: 10.17605/OSF.IO/H56G9.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support. To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of PLWNT in sleep-onset chronic insomnia and to investigate, via multimodal techniques, its modulatory effects on cerebral cortical networks. This prospective, single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3-diagnosed sleep-onset chronic insomnia, randomized 1:1 to a 12-week PLWNT or CBT-I intervention in a superiority design. The primary endpoint is the baseline-to-week-12 change in PSQI total score. Secondary measures include validated scales (ISI, PSAS, HADS, PSS, HAS, MEQ, MFI-20, GSRS, SF-36), sleep diary, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI. Exploratory mechanistic endpoints include (1) EEG-derived spectral power and wPLI within the DMN, SN, and CEN during wakefulness, sleep-onset latency, and sleep stages (N1-N3, REM), and (2) resting-state fMRI connectivity of the same networks. Clinical assessments occur at baseline (week 0), week 6, week 12 (end of intervention), and weeks 16, 20, 24, and 36 after randomization (7 time points); laboratory and imaging measures are obtained at baseline and week 12 only. Primary analysis will use generalized estimating equations on LOCF-imputed data, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. This randomized controlled trial directly compares PLWNT with CBT-I for sleep-onset chronic insomnia, integrating clinical outcome measures with neuroimaging-based mechanistic insights. The findings could position PLWNT as a non-drug therapeutic option backed by objective imaging data.

papers.title: Exercise Improves Dermal Collagen and Elastic Fibers: In Vivo Evidence From Female Volunteers and an Animal Model.
papers.abstract: With increasing interest in aesthetic appearance and skin health, direct, objective, in vivo evidence remains limited regarding whether exercise improves the structural status of dermal collagen and elastic fibers. To investigate the effects of exercise on dermal collagen and elastic fiber status. This study combined an animal experiment with a human observational study. In the animal experiment, healthy female C57BL/6J mice were divided into a middle-aged exercise group (ME, n = 10, 43 weeks old), a middle-aged sedentary group (MS, n = 5, 43 weeks old), and a young sedentary group (YS, n = 5, 6-8 weeks old). The ME group underwent 4 weeks of voluntary wheel running, whereas the MS and YS groups served as sedentary controls representing different age stages. After 4 weeks, in vivo two-photon imaging of dorsal skin was performed in all three groups. Two-photon images were quantitatively analyzed to obtain autofluorescence (AF), second harmonic generation (SHG), the SHG-to-AF aging index of dermis (SAAID), and the elastin-to-collagen ratio (ELCOR). Immunofluorescence staining for Collagen I and Elastin was performed on skin tissue from the imaging site. In the human study, a total of 156 female volunteers completed an exercise questionnaire and underwent two-photon imaging of the right zygomatic region of the face. SHG, AF, SAAID, and ELCOR were obtained using an image analysis approach consistent with that used in the animal experiment. Weekly total exercise duration (WeeklyMinutes) was calculated from the questionnaire. Participants were analyzed using both a 150 min/week grouping strategy and a median-based grouping strategy. Propensity score matching was first performed using age as the covariate, followed by multivariable regression adjustment in the matched samples. In the animal experiment, SAAID, SHG, and AF were increased and ELCOR was decreased in the ME group compared with the MS group, with several indicators shifting toward YS levels. Immunofluorescence showed stronger Collagen I- and Elastin-related signals in the ME group than in the MS group, consistent with the two-photon results. In the human study, 48 and 69 matched pairs were obtained after propensity score matching under the 150 min/week and median-based grouping strategies, respectively. The results were consistent across both grouping strategies. Higher exercise levels were associated with higher SAAID and SHG, lower ELCOR, and no significant difference in AF. After further adjustment for BMI, smoking, alcohol use, and average daily sleep duration, the overall pattern of the results remained unchanged. Using two-photon microscopy, this study provides direct, objective, in vivo evidence that exercise may favorably affect dermal collagen and elastic fibers. These findings provide experimental and population-based evidence supporting exercise as a strategy for maintaining skin health. This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registration number: ChiCTR2600123115).

papers.title: Myocardial Hmgcs2-Driven Ketogenesis Promotes Atrial Fibrillation in Diabetes.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Elevated circulating ketone bodies (β-hydroxybutyrate [β-OHB]) in T2DM are considered hepatic in origin and benefit the heart via energy provision. Although we found ketogenesis enzyme Hmgcs2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2) upregulated in both atrial and ventricular tissues of T2DM mice, alongside increased cardiac and circulating β-OHB. Whether enhanced Hmgcs2 is related to AF, ketogenesis-dependent or independent, remained unclear. T2DM mice were induced by high-fat diet and followed by streptozocin injection. Cardiac-specific Hmgcs2 overexpression and cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockout were conducted in T2DM mice. Cardiac function and left atrial diameter were evaluated using echocardiography, and cardiac electrophysiology was examined through electrical mapping. Programmed electrical stimulation was delivered to induce AF. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria of patients with or without T2DM were analyzed. The heart functioned as a primary ketogenic organ in T2DM mice via upregulating Hmgcs2, surpassing the liver. Hmgcs2-mediated shunting of fatty acid-derived acetyl-CoA into ketogenesis depleted myocardial energy reserves, exacerbated oxidative stress, and caused mitochondrial injury, ultimately increasing AF inducibility and diastolic dysfunction. In addition, cardiac-derived β-hydroxybutyrate released into circulation prolonged action potential duration in atrial cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, Hmgcs2-mediated cytosolic β-hydroxybutyrylation targeted Oxct1 (3-oxoacid CoA-transferase 1) for degradation, blocking cardiac ketolysis. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria confirmed active cardiac ketogenesis in patients with T2DM and heart-derived ketone release into systemic circulation. Venous plasma β-OHB levels positively correlated with atrial low-voltage burden and postablation AF recurrence. Cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockdown improved cardiac utilization of fatty acids, β-OHB, and glucose in T2DM mice by suppressing cardiac ketogenesis; this intervention, with reduced circulating β-OHB, attenuated diabetes-associated AF. Cardiac Hmgcs2 represented a novel therapeutic target for diabetic AF and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

papers.title: Sleep regularity associates with brain health in older adults.
papers.abstract: We examined the relationships between actigraphy-based regularity of sleep timing and brain aging outcomes among functionally unimpaired older adults. Participants included 149 older adults without dementia enrolled in studies at the University of California San Francisco. Participants completed neuropsychological testing and brain magnetic resonance imaging followed by 30 days of Fitbit Inspire 2 actigraphy monitoring to capture sleep regularity (i.e., day-to-day consistency in sleep/wake timing), average sleep duration, and variability in sleep duration. Linear regression examined cognitive and brain imaging outcomes as a function of sleep features, covarying for demographics. More consistent sleep regularity related to better global cognition, executive function, and memory; fewer depressive symptoms; larger brain volumes; fewer white matter hyperintensities; and better white matter integrity (Ps < 0.05). Sleep regularity was a stronger predictor than average sleep duration and variability in sleep duration for all outcomes. Consistency in sleep/wake timing (sleep regularity) is important for healthy brain aging.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: Venous Vascular Closure System Versus Conventional Figure of Eight Suture Following Single Shot Device Pulmonary Vein Isolation: The VASC-AF Study.
papers.abstract: Optimization of femoral venous access management has become increasingly important as catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF) continues to evolve towards greater safety with accelerated recovery pathways. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of a bioabsorbable venous vascular closure system (VCS) compared with a conventional figure-of-eight (F8) suture and manual compression following contemporary single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). VASC-AF was a prospective, multicentre, randomized controlled trial performed at three German electrophysiology centres. One hundred consecutive patients undergoing single-shot PVI were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to femoral venous closure using the VASCADE MVP VCS; (n=50) or conventional F8 suture (n=50). The primary efficacy endpoint was time to ambulation. The primary safety endpoint comprised major periprocedural adverse events requiring medical intervention before hospital discharge.Baseline characteristics and procedural variables were comparable between study groups. Median time to ambulation was significantly shorter following vascular closure with VCS compared with F8 sutures (120 [120-150] vs. 180 [180-240] min; P=0.015). Likewise, time to haemostasis (0.5 [0.5-2] vs. 1 [1-2] min; P=0.021) and time to discharge eligibility (2.5 [2.1-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-5.0] h; P=0.019) were significantly reduced.Major adverse events occurred infrequently and did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, vascular closure using VCS significantly reduced minor vascular access complications (6% vs. 26%; P=0.006), groin pain, and patient discomfort while improving overall post-procedural satisfaction. Among patients undergoing contemporary single-shot AF ablation, use of a bioabsorbable VCS significantly accelerated post-procedural recovery while maintaining a comparable major safety profile. Reduced access-site complications and improved patient-reported outcomes support VCS as an important component of enhanced recovery pathways following AF ablation especially in an ambulatory or Same-Day Discharge setting.
