papers.title: Loss of the clock protein PERIOD1 causes sex-specific impacts on the heart in Dahl salt-sensitive rats.
papers.abstract: Salt-sensitive (SS) hypertension is a driver of cardiovascular disease. Circadian biology is implicated in hypertension. One component of the circadian molecular clock, the protein PERIOD1 (PER1), is involved in blood pressure regulation. We previously published that loss of PER1 (PER1 KO) in a rat model of SS hypertension, the Dahl SS rat, is associated with exacerbated renal injury and hypertension, as well as disrupted circadian regulation of heart rate. The cardiac and sex-specific impacts of PER1 KO in SS hypertension are undetermined. We utilized male and female PER1 KO and Dahl SS rats to investigate changes in the cardiac transcriptome, revealing sex-dependent shifts in gene expression. Male PER1 KO rats exhibited upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling. Consistent with this, male, but not female PER1 KO rats showed higher cardiac fibrosis compared to their Dahl SS counterparts. Terminal measurements revealed that male, but not female PER1 KO rats had increased blood pressure compared to Dahl SS controls. Given the lack of an apparent phenotype in females, only male subjects were used for subsequent ultrasound echocardiography studies. We determined longitudinal in vivo cardiac function in male rats during normal salt and 14 days of high salt diet. This revealed reduced stroke volume and decreased cardiac output at baseline, prior to exposure to high salt diet in male PER1 KO rats. These results indicate that impaired cardiac function may predispose PER1 KO rats to salt-sensitive hypertension.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

papers.title: Aβ42 induces selective degeneration in hippocampal cells of aged monkeys.
papers.abstract: The hippocampus is one of the earliest and most severely affected brain regions in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is critical for memory formation. However, the precise mechanisms through which AD disrupts hippocampal neurons remain poorly understood. To investigate the effects of Aβ42 in a model closer to humans, we performed stereotaxic injections of an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector encoding human Aβ42 into the hippocampus of young (7-year-old) and aged (>20-year-old) cynomolgus monkeys. We found that AAV9-mediated Aβ42 expression induced more severe neuropathology, reduced daytime activity, and increased sleep disturbances in aged monkeys compared to young controls. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed an age-dependent reduction in disease-associated microglia subtype II (DAM II) in the aged hippocampus. Furthermore, we identified a specific subtype of hippocampal pyramidal neurons (PCs) ( TRPS1 + RELN +) that is selectively vulnerable to Aβ42 toxicity in aged monkeys. Our findings indicate that Aβ42 toxicity is exacerbated in the aged primate hippocampus due to a combination of microglial decline and the selective vulnerability of a distinct neuronal subtype ( TRPS1 + RELN + PCs). This identified subtype represents a new potential therapeutic target for treating hippocampal dysfunction in AD.

papers.title: Prototype-based geometry of local object patches in the pigeon mesopallium ventrolaterale.
papers.abstract: In natural vision, objects are frequently partially occluded and thus perceived through local fragments, yet how such fragments are organized in neural representational space remains poorly understood. Using pigeons ( Columba livia) as a model, we combined behavior from a whole-part image categorization paradigm with population electrophysiological recordings from the mesopallium ventrolaterale (MVL) during passive viewing. We used Contrastive Embedding for Behavioral and Representational Analysis-time (CEBRA) to embed neural time series into a low-dimensional space, defined category neural prototypes from population responses to whole images, and projected local patches into the same space to quantify their distances to the prototypes. This framework allowed systematic tests of how prototype distance relates to behavioral accuracy and patch semantics. In MVL, animal categories formed compact, prototype-centered clusters. Across patches, greater prototype distance predicted lower behavioral accuracy, and patches closer to the prototype were enriched for diagnostic semantic parts (e.g., heads and faces). By contrast, across multiple deep-network baselines, prototype distance neither reliably predicted behavior nor consistently reflected the semantic distribution of patches. Building on these baselines, we then introduced a local prototype learning mechanism in which category matching is governed by the proximity between local features and learned prototypes. The resulting network reproduced several MVL-consistent geometric signatures, including prototype-centered clustering for animal categories and a negative relationship between prototype distance and behavior. Together, these results support the hypothesis that incomplete-object representations in pigeon MVL are organized by a diagnostic-part-related prototype geometry, and suggest that this geometry provides actionable neural constraints for brain-inspired vision models.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.abstract: Permanent night-shift work induces circadian misalignment, sleep disruption, and impaired physiological organization. Although exercise is increasingly recognized as a non-photic zeitgeber, its long-term association with circadian adaptation under occupational conditions remains poorly understood. To examine whether habitual physical activity and a 12-week supervised exercise program are associated with circadian organization, sleep, and physiological rhythms in permanent night-shift workers. Study 1 was a cross-sectional comparison of 12 habitually physically active and 12 sedentary permanent night-shift workers matched for major demographic and occupational characteristics. Study 2 was an uncontrolled longitudinal before-after intervention in 16 initially sedentary workers. Using the same ambulatory protocol, activity-rest rhythms, oral temperature, sleep, and neuromuscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, and cognitive variables were repeatedly assessed across an entire work-rest cycle. Habitually physically active workers exhibited greater rhythm amplitude, dominant oscillatory periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization across several physiological systems than sedentary workers. Similar pre-to-post changes were observed in Study 2. During weekend recovery, dominant oscillatory periods transiently shortened to approximately 18-22 h, concurrently with rapid repositioning of activity-rest and oral-temperature acrophases toward diurnal timing. These dynamics most likely reflect adaptive circadian reorganization rather than changes in endogenous circadian period. Regular physical activity was associated with greater circadian robustness, temporal coherence, and better sleep. Because Study 2 lacked a control group, the longitudinal changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the exercise program. Controlled studies using direct phase markers are required.

papers.title: Biopsychosocial Network Associations in Paediatric Chronic Pain: A Cross-Lagged Panel Network Study.
papers.abstract: Biopsychosocial models of chronic pain emphasize interactions between biological, psychological and social processes, yet little is known about their organization over time in paediatric chronic pain. This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal network associations among pain intensity, pain interference, pain extent, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, pain catastrophizing, sleep disturbance, fatigue and peer relationships in children and adolescents with chronic pain. The baseline network was estimated using a Gaussian graphical model with regularized partial correlations (N = 744). Cross-lagged panel network models were used to examine autoregressive and cross-lagged associations from baseline to 12 months (n = 357) and 24 months (n = 186) among youth with persistent chronic pain. Pain interference had the highest cross-sectional strength centrality, followed by depressive and anxiety symptoms. Strongest baseline associations involved fatigue-pain interference, anxiety-depressive symptoms, pain catastrophizing-anxiety symptoms and sleep disturbance-pain interference. In the longitudinal models, pain interference showed the most consistent prospective pattern, with associations to later pain catastrophizing at 12 months and to later sleep disturbance and pain catastrophizing at 24 months. Depressive symptoms and pain catastrophizing were more often associated with prior levels of other domains. Findings extend prior cross-sectional evidence by showing that pain interference was highly connected at baseline and prospectively involved among youth with persistent chronic pain. Pain interference may represent an informative functional domain for understanding how pain-related, psychological and physical difficulties are organized over time, supporting the clinical relevance of assessing interference with daily functioning. This study extends paediatric chronic pain research by examining cross-sectional and longitudinal associations among pain-related, psychological, physical and social domains. Pain interference showed the highest connectivity at baseline and was consistently involved in prospective associations, particularly with pain catastrophizing and sleep disturbance. These findings highlight multidomain assessment and suggest that interference with daily functioning may help identify broader pain-related difficulties that could otherwise be missed.

papers.title: Association of questionnaire-defined probable obstructive sleep apnea with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in US adults: a NHANES study with machine learning analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome integrates cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, and metabolic dysfunction within a prevention-oriented framework, but the population-level association between obstructive sleep apnea and advanced CKM remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 8,523 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between questionnaire-defined probable OSA (pOSA) and advanced CKM, with subgroup analyses and interaction tests performed across predefined population groups. Six machine learning models were also developed for exploratory classification of advanced CKM, and Shapley Additive Explanations were used to interpret the selected model. pOSA was more common among participants with advanced CKM than among those with non-advanced stages. In the core multivariable-adjusted survey-weighted model, pOSA was associated with higher odds of advanced CKM; however, after additional adjustment for body mass index categories, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.92-1.49, p = 0.197). In the machine learning analysis, XGBoost had the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.876), whereas the random forest model showed favorable calibration with an area under the curve of 0.868 and was selected for interpretation. Age contributed most to the model output, followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate, smoking, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, glycated hemoglobin, and mean systolic blood pressure. These findings suggest a potential association between pOSA and advanced CKM syndrome among United States adults, while highlighting the importance of considering adiposity when interpreting this association.

papers.title: Association between obstructive sleep apnea and severe exertional dyspnea in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Exertional dyspnea is a common and disabling symptom of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The severity of dyspnea may not correspond closely to spirometric impairment. In patients with COPD and coexisting obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), recurrent nocturnal desaturation may represent an additional sleep-related feature relevant to severe exertional dyspnea. We included 758 clinically stable patients with COPD. Severe exertional dyspnea was defined as a modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale (mMRC) score ≥3. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the associations of the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation index (ODI), and percentage of sleep time with oxygen saturation below 90% (T90) with severe exertional dyspnea. Participants were predominantly male (92.2%), with a median age of 67.0 years. Severe exertional dyspnea was present in 199 patients (26.3%). After adjusting for confounders, ODI ≥15 was significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.14-2.51, p = 0.009). In contrast, neither AHI ≥15 nor T90 ≥ 10% showed a statistically significant association. In continuous analyses, log(ODI + 1) remained significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.03-1.57, p = 0.025), whereas log(AHI + 1) and log(T90 + 1) were not statistically significant. Nocturnal ODI was independently associated with severe exertional dyspnea, whereas AHI and T90 were not. The more consistent association for ODI suggests that recurrent nocturnal oxygen desaturations may provide clinically relevant information about the OSA-related component of symptom burden beyond respiratory-event frequency or cumulative nocturnal hypoxemia.

papers.title: Network architecture of sleep, biomarkers, and cognition: Rapid eye movement sleep latency as a cross-domain connector.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD) pathology and cognitive decline, but how sleep architecture, biomarkers, and cognition are organized within a conditional dependence framework remains unclear. We studied 98 adults spanning normal cognition (NC; n = 21), mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 34), and clinically diagnosed AD dementia (n = 43) using overnight polysomnography, plasma phosphorylated tau181 (p-tau181), neurofilament light chain (NfL), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), amyloid-β positron emission tomography (PET), and multidomain cognitive testing. A regularized Gaussian graphical model was used to characterize conditional associations and identify cross-domain connectivity among sleep, biomarkers, and cognition. The 17-variable network contained 26 edges, with significantly denser within-domain than cross-domain connectivity (40.5% vs 9.6%; p < 0.001). Direct sleep-cognition connections were sparse. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep latency had the highest bridge strength (0.387), directly connecting the sleep domain with NfL, amyloid-β PET, and BDNF. Plasma p-tau181 was the only biomarker directly connected to global cognition. Exploratory mediation analyses were consistent with indirect associations involving p-tau181 in three of five cognitive domains. Sleep architecture and cognition were conditionally linked primarily through biomarker nodes. REM sleep latency and plasma p-tau181 may represent key cross-domain connectors linking sleep architecture, neurodegeneration, and cognition across the AD continuum.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: Sleep-cognition associations change direction with proximity to dementia diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Differentiating aspects of sleep health that are modifiable risk factors from prodromal symptoms or consequences of dementia can inform dementia prevention and/or clinical screening efforts, and temporal mapping of sleep-cognition associations can further inform mechanistic hypotheses regarding the role of sleep leading up to dementia diagnosis. We examined bidirectional associations between cognitive function and three modifiable sleep health features, and whether these associations vary by proximity to dementia diagnosis. 291 preclinical dementia participants (median initial age = 83 years, 73% female) and 281 matched cognitively unimpaired 'controls' from the Rush Memory and Aging Project completed up to 11 annual assessments of global cognition (composite of 19 neuropsychological measures) and actigraphy-derived measures of sleep amount, regularity, and timing. Linear mixed-effects models tested whether bidirectional sleep-cognition relationships differed by years-to-dementia diagnosis (preclinical dementia sample) or years-to-last follow-up (matched controls) after adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates. In the preclinical dementia sample, time-to-dementia modified the effects of sleep amount (both β = 0.02) and regularity (-0.04 < β < 0.02), but not timing, on next-year global cognition. Ten years before dementia diagnosis, longer and more irregular sleep predicted better next-year cognition; 1 year before diagnosis, these sleep patterns predicted worse next-year cognition. While sleep amount unidirectionally predicted subsequent cognition, sleep regularity-cognition associations were consistently bidirectional. These patterns were not observed in matched controls. Changes in sleep-cognition associations over time may differentiate preclinical dementia from normal aging. Future research should investigate the driving mechanisms and modifiability of these sleep-cognition associations.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: Thermal regulation of ant colonies is driven by biological rhythms and acclimation.
papers.abstract: Activity in hot environments is physiologically costly for ectotherms. In social insect colonies, the division of labor may reduce the costs of physiological performance. Additional mechanisms may include plastic responses to thermal conditions and rhythmic investment into thermal tolerance. Here, we evaluate the extent to which static specialization, biological rhythms, and acclimation account for short-term shifts in thermal performance using a pair of complementary experiments in the tropical ant Ectatomma ruidum. In the first experiment, we marked foraging workers at distinct time periods with differing temperatures, and then compared the thermal tolerance of these workers and non-foragers with a time-to-failure knockdown assay. In the second experiment, we subdivided colonies into three laboratory nests under contrasting thermal regimes and performed the assay at daily thermal minima and maxima. We found thermal tolerance was governed both by acclimation and a daily rhythm. These plastic shifts in thermal tolerance were more substantial than differences among specialized workers. These colonies primarily responded to thermal challenges by flexible changes in thermal tolerance rather than the static differences associated with the division of labor. Our findings demonstrate how modular biological systems may demonstrate greater capacity for resilience to increasing variability in thermal challenges.

papers.title: Does Smoking Cause Obstructive Sleep Apnea? New Longitudinal Evidence Challenges Assumptions.
papers.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

papers.title: Rapid and Controlled Single-Nanopore Insertion via Hydrogel-Confined Localized Delivery.
papers.abstract: Controlled insertion of a single protein pore, also referred to as a nanopore, into a free-standing lipid bilayer underpins high-resolution single-channel electrophysiology. Hitherto, conventional bulk reconstitution is stochastic, slow, and prone to multiple insertions. To overcome this, we adapted a hydrogel-confined delivery strategy in which an agarose-filled glass capillary delivers nanopores directly to the bilayer. An optimal window of agarose concentration, aerolysin concentration, and membrane potential raised the single-pore yield to >70% and shortened the waiting time to the first insertion from tens of minutes to a few minutes, without altering native pore conductance. The approach generalizes across the β-barrel toxin aerolysin, the mitochondrial TOM core complex, and a DNA nanopore, making nanopore insertion rapid, controlled, and reproducible.

papers.title: Spreading voltage buildup in high density EEG during migraine aura: A longitudinal single-patient study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate spreading features in surface high-density electroencephalogram (HD-EEG) during migraine aura. Approximately 20%-30% of people with migraine experience migraine with aura (MwA). Migraine aura consists of transient neurological deficits such as visual, sensory, speech, motor, brainstem, or retinal symptoms. Clear features of cortical spreading depolarization (CSD) during migraine aura have recently been demonstrated using intracranial depth electrodes in a patient with MwA and comorbid epilepsy; however, in patients with MwA without comorbid epilepsy, direct detection of CSD in a non-invasive setting is still lacking. We report a longitudinal 256-channel HD-EEG study with a direct coupled amplifier set-up in a 45-year-old patient with MwA, in whom repeated recordings could be acquired during aura including early phases and interictally. Electrodes over the forehead, cheeks, periauricular, and nuchal regions were removed to reduce muscle artifacts, resulting in 172 electrodes. In total, 14 electroencephalograms (EEGs) were acquired, thereof eight during the ictal phase. In two out of four aura recordings with predominantly right homonymous scintillating scotoma, recorded soon after onset, we observed a spreading voltage buildup with contralateral maximum. This was associated with a spreading power increase in the delta frequency band. Voltage increases between neighboring electrodes showed a spread with velocity of estimated at 3.8 mm/min. During auras, increased voltage was observed, predominantly in occipital and temporal electrodes. We suggest that topographically related amplitude buildup and delta spread in temporal relation with aura progression reflects CSD. Since invasive CSD detection has been suggested as a useful neuromonitoring tool, with prognostic and therapeutic relevance, further confirmatory studies for non-invasive CSD detections are warranted.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population. To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach. Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing. Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.

papers.title: Beyond the RMMA Index: Respiratory-Event Context and Episode Duration in Adults With Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Sleep Bruxism.
papers.abstract: Sleep bruxism (SB) frequently coexists with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). However, whether rhythmic masticatory muscle activity (RMMA) reflects respiratory recovery, an airway response, or an independent motor phenomenon remains unclear. To characterize the respiratory-event context and duration of RMMA in adults with OSA and SB. Polysomnographic data from 94 adults with OSA and SB were retrospectively analysed. Each RMMA episode was matched to the nearest respiratory event and classified within a 20 s window as pre-respiratory, respiratory-overlap, or post-respiratory; episodes beyond 20 s were considered temporally unrelated. A circular-shift null model assessed whether RMMA-respiratory proximity exceeded within-night chance expectations. Bayesian multinomial mixed-effects models compared RMMA temporal contexts across respiratory-event types, and mixed-effects models assessed arousal linkage and RMMA duration across temporal contexts. Exploratory analyses examined associations between RMMA expression measures and polysomnographic variables. Among 3774 RMMA episodes, 2686 (71.2%) were temporally related to respiratory events, exceeding chance expectations (0.733 vs. 0.273; p < 0.001). Compared with obstructive apnea-related RMMA, central apnea-related RMMA showed higher odds of being pre-respiratory (OR 2.67, 95% CrI 1.76-4.19) and respiratory-overlap (OR 3.26, 95% CrI 2.03-5.29). Of post-respiratory RMMA episodes, 486 (43.0%) occurred within 5 s of respiratory-related arousal onset. Shorter RMMA episode duration was associated with greater respiratory, oxygen desaturation and arousal burden. In this predominantly male, relatively young OSA-SB cohort, RMMA showed heterogeneous temporal organization and RMMA episode duration showed exploratory associations with OSA-related physiological burden.

papers.title: Proposed profile-informed rehabilitation framework for cardiometabolic risk after elite sport retirement: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Retirement from elite sport can alter training, energy balance, pain, sleep, identity and structured support. Evidence is concentrated in selected male Western cohorts and remains fragmented across weight, metabolic, sleep, rhythm, women's-health and rehabilitation domains. We mapped both cardiometabolic patterns and population-level evidence gaps after elite-sport retirement. A formal corrective search covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection from database inception through 14 July 2026. The review was retrospectively registered on OSF. Human title/abstract screening routed 287 records to full text; 162 retrieved reports received named human review and cross-review. Evidence was classified as direct retired-athlete (D), contextual athlete (C), general guidance/tool support (G), background (B) or author-proposed inference (P) and synthesised narratively. The searches produced 4,884 unique records. Of 286 unique report units sought for retrieval, 162 were retrieved and human-assessed, 21 were excluded and 141 were included; 124 were not retrieved and were not counted as eligibility exclusions. The included set comprised 102 new independent primary cohorts, 20 linked reports and 19 evidence syntheses. Non-mutually-exclusive charting identified 78 reports on cardiovascular structure/function/events, 68 on adiposity/body composition/weight, 59 on conventional metabolic risk, 50 on mortality/longevity and 17 on sleep-disordered breathing. The evidence suggested coexistence between favourable population-average longevity and less favourable weight, metabolic, sleep or cardiovascular findings in selected exposure profiles. Retired women, Asian and other non-Western athletes, combat- and weight-class athletes and para-athletes remained underrepresented. Post-retirement cardiometabolic evidence is heterogeneous but clinically and scientifically informative. A proposed profile-informed framework may organise weight and activity trajectories, conventional risk factors, symptoms and sport/exposure history without treating profile labels as biological classes. The framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation; it does not establish athlete-specific thresholds, fixed follow-up intervals or referral rules. Retrospective registration, non-duplicated title/abstract screening, incomplete retrieval and charting and the absence of auditable formal risk-of-bias ratings warrant cautious interpretation. Open Science Framework, retrospectively registered after initial submission, 16 May 2026 (A9J5Y; doi: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/A9J5Y ).

papers.title: The association between sedentary behavior and eye diseases: a prospective study from the UK Biobank.
papers.abstract: Sedentary behavior (SB) is a well-established risk factor for multiple chronic diseases. However, evidence regarding its association with common ocular disorders remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigated the prospective associations between SB and the risks of incident age-related macular degeneration (AMD), glaucoma, dry eye disease (DED), and retinal vein occlusion (RVO). We conducted a prospective cohort analysis using data from the UK Biobank. Separate analytical cohorts were established for AMD (n = 374,552), glaucoma (n = 370,997), DED (n = 374,398), and RVO (n = 374,924). During a median follow-up of approximately 14.04 years, 7,266 AMD, 8,112 glaucoma, 452 DED, and 786 RVO cases were identified. Pre-existing ocular diseases were identified using ICD-10 records and self-reported diagnoses. Incident AMD, glaucoma, and RVO were identified from ICD-10 records, whereas incident DED was identified by self-report. Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses, interaction analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed. In unadjusted models, higher SB was associated with increased risks of AMD, glaucoma, DED and RVO. After multivariable adjustment, only a borderline statistically significant association remained for AMD (HR = 1.01; 95% CI: 1.00-1.02), whereas no significant associations were observed for glaucoma, DED, or RVO. RCS analyses demonstrated mild J-shaped associations between SB and AMD and glaucoma, with the lowest risk observed at approximately 3.7 h/day; however, these associations became nonsignificant after full adjustment. Stratified interaction analyses identified significant effect modification for AMD by body mass index (BMI), glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), and physical activity (PA) level, and for DED by sex and BMI. Sensitivity analyses, including additional adjustment for physical activity and sleep duration and analyses of domain-specific sedentary behaviors, did not alter the overall conclusions. After adjustment for potential confounders, no statistically significant independent associations were observed between SB and incident AMD, glaucoma, DED, or RVO. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence against a causal relationship. Further studies incorporating objective exposure assessment, repeated measurements, and causal inference approaches are warranted to clarify the potential role of sedentary behavior in ocular disease development.

papers.title: Association of Nonpharmacologic Therapies with Health-Related Quality-of-Life Outcomes in Patients with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Nonpharmacologic therapies (NPTs) are recommended as first-line treatment for chronic low back pain (CLBP). A retrospective cohort study was conducted within a national pain research registry from April 2016 through April 2025. Patients with CLBP reported use of exercise therapy, yoga, massage therapy, spinal manipulation, and acupuncture at enrollment and at quarterly intervals through 12 months. Health-related quality-of-life (HRQOL) outcomes for physical function, anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep disturbance, participation in social roles, and pain interference were collected at enrollment and quarterly intervals. Generalized estimating equations were used to measure HRQOL outcomes associated with each NPT and a series of potential confounders. The magnitude of the standardized mean difference (SMD) between users and nonusers of each NPT was used to assess the clinical importance of the results. A total of 723 (40.4%) of 1789 study patients used at least one NPT at enrollment. Exercise therapy was associated with less fatigue (SMD, 0.06) and sleep disturbance (SMD, 0.07), and yoga was associated with better physical function (SMD, 0.06) and greater participation in social roles (0.06) over 12 months. None of these results approached the threshold for clinical importance. Users of massage therapy, spinal manipulation, and acupuncture did not report better outcomes than nonusers on any HRQOL measure. In multivariable analyses, greater pain self-efficacy was consistently associated with better outcomes across all HRQOL measures, whereas greater pain catastrophizing was often associated with worse outcomes. None of the NPTs for CLBP yielded clinically important differences between users and nonusers over 12 months. These findings have important clinical implications in the management of CLBP because each studied NPT is recommended in major clinical practice guidelines and commonly used by patients.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine

papers.title: Trajectories of Sleep and Pain From the Perioperative Period to One-Year After Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality and pain are closely related, and surgery is known to impair sleep quality temporarily. Yet the effects of daily fluctuations in sleep and pain and their impact on long-term outcomes remain insufficiently explored. This prospective cohort study explored bidirectional day-to-day associations between sleep and pain and preoperative predictors of one-year pain outcomes. A total of 171 patients with osteoarthritis scheduled for knee arthroplasty were enrolled. Preoperative assessments included sleep quality, symptoms of anxiety and depression, lifestyle evaluation, and pain intensity. For the first week after surgery, patients reported daily sleep quality and pain intensity. After 1 year, knee pain intensity was reassessed. One hundred and twenty-five patients completed preoperative assessments, 89 completed all seven postoperative daily assessments, and 112 responded after 1 year. Pain peaked on postoperative day two and was significantly lower than preoperative levels at 1 year (p < 0.05). Daily fluctuations in pain and sleep were bidirectionally correlated: higher pain intensity predicted poorer sleep quality the following night (p < 0.05), while poor sleep quality predicted higher next-day pain intensities (p < 0.05). Patients in the worst quartiles of pain and sleep during the first postoperative week reported significantly higher one-year postoperative pain compared to those in the best quartiles (p < 0.05). Preoperative positive affect, with non-significant contributions from sleep quality and symptoms of anxiety, predicted 13.1% (adjusted R2 10.2%) of the variance in one-year postoperative pain. In conclusion, sleep, pain, and psychological factors in the perioperative period are relevant for long-term pain outcomes after knee arthroplasty.

papers.title: Surgical outcomes in stereoelectroencephalography versus subdural grids: a systematic review & meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Invasive extra-operative monitoring for drug-resistant epilepsy is primarily conducted using stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) and subdural grids (SDG). This study aims to provide a comprehensive comparison of the two methods. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Database. The primary outcomes assessed included postoperative seizure outcome, complications, neurological deficits, and pain. All original English-language studies published up until January 2025 were reviewed, and the risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Seven studies involving a total of 1,156 patients who underwent SEEG and 737 patients who underwent SDG were included. The pooled analysis demonstrated higher odds of seizure freedom in the SEEG group compared with the SDG group (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.33-2.22). However, the included studies compared clinically distinct patient populations with different indications for invasive monitoring and surgical pathways, which may have influenced seizure outcomes. Across the included studies, SEEG was consistently associated with lower infection rates and reduced postoperative analgesic requirements, while rates of hemorrhage and neurological deficits were generally comparable between groups, with some studies reporting slightly higher hemorrhage rates in SEEG cohorts. SEEG was associated with higher odds of seizure freedom following epilepsy surgery; however, this finding should be interpreted with caution because the included studies compared clinically distinct patient populations with different indications for invasive monitoring, surgical pathways, and resection rates. The available evidence suggests lower infection rates and reduced postoperative analgesic requirements with SEEG, whereas findings regarding hemorrhage and neurological deficits were variable across studies. Further studies with larger, more comparable patient populations are needed to better define procedure-specific risks and outcomes.

papers.title: Predicting others' actions through one's own motor style: Behavioral and neural evidence for a kinematic similarity effect.
papers.abstract: Predictive processes during action observation are known to benefit from motor expertise, but it remains unclear which factors drive successful prediction in everyday actions, where everyone can be considered an "expert." We hypothesized that prediction accuracy is modulated not only by expertise per se, but by the degree of fine-grained kinematic overlap between the observer's and the agent's motor repertoire, here operationalized as motor similarity. In Study 1 (N = 90, action execution), we introduced a continuous, multidimensional, kinematics-based metric of inter-individual motor distance, and used it to quantify each participant's motor style relative to others. In Study 2 (N = 20, behavioral) and Study 3 (N = 21, behavioral and EEG), we then tailored action-observation tasks to each participant by selecting movements that varied parametrically in similarity to their own motor style, while verifying that stimuli across similarity levels carried equivalent amounts of action-relevant kinematic information. Behavioral results consistently showed that motor similarity enhances perceptual prediction: observers were more accurate when viewing actions that were closer to their individual motor style. Electrophysiological data further revealed that beta-band modulation, a neural signature associated with prediction uncertainty, is amplified over sensorimotor regions when participants observed more dissimilar movements. Together, these findings demonstrate that the degree of agent-observer kinematic overlap is a key determinant of prediction processes, extending beyond traditional expertise-based accounts.

papers.title: Differential effects of α-synuclein aggregates on the electrophysiology of SNpc vs VTA dopaminergic neurons in acute mouse slices.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterised by the early loss of dopaminergic neurons (DNs) in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) with other DNs more resistant. Aggregation of alpha synuclein (α-Syn) appears to be a major driver of pathology. We have investigated the differential effects of intracellular α-Syn aggregates on the electrophysiology of SNpc and VTA DNs in acute slices. Introduction of α-Syn aggregates into single SNpc DNs increased whole-cell conductance and altered firing, effects partially reversed by the KATP channel inhibitor glibenclamide. These effects were either absent or much weaker in VTA DNs. Although diazoxide (KATP channel opener) had little effect on VTA DNs compared to SNpc, the effects were significantly enhanced by α-Syn aggregates. These findings demonstrate that acute introduction of α-Syn aggregates significantly changes the electrophysiological properties of SNpc DNs, which is mediated in part by the presence of KATP channels, with these effects much reduced in VTA DNs.

papers.title: Longitudinal resting-state EEG-based modeling predicts phenoconversion and delineates heterogeneity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder is a high-risk prodromal syndrome for Lewy body diseases but highly heterogeneous. Neurophysiologic markers resolving this heterogeneity and predicting phenoconversion remain limited. We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) modeling to longitudinal resting-state EEG from a prospective cohort of 285 participants. SuStaIn identified a progressive degenerative subtype (Subtype 2), characterized by delta/theta increases and lower MoCA scores, and a posterior beta-low subtype (Subtype 1), which was longitudinally unstable and of uncertain independent prognostic significance. Longitudinal validation demonstrated substantial subtype shifting in Subtype 1 and stage advancement predominantly in Subtype 2. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, subtype shifting and accelerated annual stage advancement (ΔStage≥2) identified individuals at exceptionally high phenoconversion risk with survival approaching 0-15% by 7.5 years. These findings extend SuStaIn beyond cross-sectional inference by incorporating longitudinal subtype-shifting and stage-advancement features to stratify prodromal heterogeneity and predict neurodegenerative progression.

papers.title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects.
papers.abstract: Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Successful memory formation is associated with reduced alpha/beta power and increased eye movements. However, their coupling and combined contribution to memory formation remain largely unknown. Across four experiments combining eye tracking with scalp or intracranial electroencephalography during free or constrained viewing, we identify the degree of visual exploration, rather than subsequent memory performance, as consistent modulator of posterior alpha/beta power. Going beyond correlations, manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from memory. Together with the finding that saccade parameters predicted alpha/beta dynamics, our results directly link posterior alpha/beta activity to the oculomotor system. Moreover, the accumulation of saccades over time accounted for reduced alpha/beta power, resembling the canonical post-stimulus alpha/beta pattern. Our work demonstrates that posterior alpha/beta activity strongly reflects eye movements, supporting alternative perspectives on alpha/beta subsequent memory effects and the general function of posterior alpha/beta activity.

papers.title: Early-Age alcohol initiation increases the risk of mental disorders in children and adolescents: a longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract: Although alcohol use is proved to relate with poor psychiatric outcomes, the longitudinal impact of early-age alcohol initiation on youth mental health is poorly characterized. The current study analyzed semi-structured interview data on substance use collected at baseline and over two years of follow-up (6, 12, 18, and 24 months) as part of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study. Participants that reported having at least one sip were defined as alcohol experimenters. Latent class trajectory model (LCTM) was used to characterize sipping patterns over follow-up period. In this study, 1659 alcohol experimenters were identified (mean age at baseline, 9.55 ± 0.50 years; 944 males [56.9%]) and matched with 1659 controls without any alcohol use. Early-age alcohol initiation was associated with higher risk of developing mental disorders (MDs, OR 1.25, [95% CI, 1.03-1.52]). Subgroup analyses suggested that pre-baseline alcohol exposure could increase the risk of sleep-wake disorder (OR 1.39, [95%CI, 1.06-1.82]), bipolar disorder (OR 1.70, [95%CI, 1.10-2.67]), non-suicidal self-injury behavior (OR 1.91, [95% CI, 1.20-3.08]) and suicidal ideation (OR 1.51, [95% CI, 1.22-2.15]). Two sipping patterns were identified among follow-up alcohol experimenters: increased sipping (Class 1, 56.7%) and decreased sipping (Class 2, 43.3%) over the two-year follow-up period. Compared with controls, only Class 1 was significantly associated with increased risk of MDs (OR 1.48, [95% CI, 1.02-2.14]). Both Class 1 and Class 2 showed elevated risk of suicidal ideation (Class1: OR 2.38, [95%CI, 1.22-4.71]; Class2: OR 2.64, [95%CI, 1.29-5.44]). These findings suggest an association between early alcohol exposure and negative mental health conditions in children aged under 12 years, highlighting children as a potential priority population for alcohol prevention efforts.

papers.title: Does orthognathic surgery increase the risk of obstructive sleep apnoea?
papers.abstract: The objective of this prospective cohort study was to evaluate longitudinal changes in the risk of obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and subjective sleep quality in healthy adults following orthognathic surgery to correct Class II and Class III dentoskeletal deformities. Seventy healthy adult subjects were assessed using the STOP-BANG Questionnaire (SBQ), Berlin Questionnaire (BQ), and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) approximately 1 month preoperatively (T0), 6 months postoperatively (T1), and 1 year postoperatively (T2). All procedures were performed by a single oral and maxillofacial surgeon over a 2-year period at two tertiary academic centres. Subjects with Class II discrepancies, predominantly treated with mandibular or bimaxillary advancement, demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in OSA risk at both 6 months and 1 year postoperatively based on SBQ (P = 0.012 and P = 0.046, respectively) and BQ scores (P = 0.012 and P = 0.007, respectively). No statistically significant differences in ESS scores were observed at either postoperative interval (P = 0.15 and P = 0.26, respectively). In contrast, subjects with Class III discrepancies, most of whom underwent bimaxillary surgery, did not exhibit a statistically significant increase in OSA risk or daytime sleepiness following surgery. Within the 1-year interval evaluated, orthognathic surgery did not increase the screening-based risk of OSA in healthy adults.

papers.title: Epidemiology and Modifiable Risk Factors for Benign Prostatic Enlargement and Related Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Benign prostatic enlargement (BPE) and related lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS/BPE) represent highly prevalent health issues globally, and related modifiable risk factors are recognized as a sensitive topic for prevention strategies. We summarized evidence on associations between the epidemiology of these conditions and modifiable risk factors. We performed a systematic review with meta-analysis of studies in MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols. Twenty-four studies (four cohort and 20 cross-sectional) were included. Pooled synthesis showed positive associations between waist circumference (WC) >90 cm (two studies) and body mass index >24 kg/m2 (three studies) and prevalent BPE in Asian males. WC >90 cm was positively associated with prevalent moderate-to-severe LUTS in the same ethnicity (two studies). Narrative synthesis showed associations between abnormal adiposity and prevalent BPE/moderate-to-severe LUTS also in non-Asian males as well as associations between the epidemiology of LUTS and physical activity, alcohol intake, metabolic syndrome, and smoking status in both ethnicities. Associations between dietary/sleep patterns and LUTS epidemiology were evident in Asian males. The certainty of evidence was very low. BPE and related LUTS represent highly prevalent health issues with global incidence and prevalence rates projected to increase in the next decade. Positive associations between high adiposity indices and prevalent BPE have been observed in both Asian and non-Asian males. Modifiable risk factors associated with moderate-to-severe LUTS include: abnormal adiposity indices, levels of physical activity, smoking status, alcohol intake, metabolic syndrome (all in both ethnicities), and sleep/dietary patterns (in Asian males). However, definitive clinical recommendations could not be provided.

papers.title: [Clinical study on heart rate variability characteristics and associated factors in critically ill patients].
papers.abstract: To evaluate the characteristics of heart rate variability (HRV) in critically ill patients and to explore its related influencing factors. A cross-sectional survey study was conducted. Critically ill patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Tianjin Medical University General Hospital between March and April 2025 were enrolled. General information of the patients including demographic characteristics, disease factors, drug factors, etc. was collected. Resting electrocardiographic signals were acquired using electrocardiographic monitoring devices during daytime (08:01-20:00) and nighttime (20:01-08:00 the next day). Time-domain indices of HRV, including standard deviation of all normal sinus R-R intervals (SDNN) and root mean square of successive differences in adjacent R-R intervals (RMSSD), frequency-domain indices, including low frequency (LF), high frequency (HF), and LF/HF ratio, as well as deceleration capacity of heart rate (DC), were extracted and computed. The diurnal variation characteristics of HRV were compared, and multiple linear regression analysis was used to identify influencing factors of HRV changes. A total of 210 critically ill patients were finally included, predominantly male [125 cases (59.5%)], with a relatively advanced age [(62.28±17.11) years] and a high proportion of comorbidities [161 cases (76.7%)]; 54.3% (114/210) had undergone surgery, with the highest proportion being within 24 hours postoperatively [69 cases (32.9%)]; the proportions of patients receiving mechanical ventilation, having indwelling catheters, or receiving sedatives/analgesics or vasoactive agents were relatively low [they were 39.0% (82/210), 48.1% (101/210), 31.0% (65/210), 32.9% (69/210), 48.6% (102/210), respectively]. All HRV parameters in critically ill patients were at low levels: SDNN was 14.57 (8.91, 24.30) ms, RMSSD was 8.75 (6.09, 14.94) ms, LF was 18.47 (6.04, 68.63) ms2, HF was 11.12 (4.91, 42.55) ms2, the LF/HF ratio was 1.67 (0.78, 3.59), and DC was 2.80 (1.90, 4.59) ms, indicating suppressed autonomic nervous function in critically ill patients, without statistically significant circadian differences in any HRV index (all P>0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis revealed that female [odds ratio (OR)=-0.162, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was -4.263 to -0.358, P=0.021], suffering from organ failure (OR=-0.229, 95%CI was -5.520 to -1.173, P=0.003), presence of one comorbidity (OR=-0.237, 95%CI was -5.822 to -0.877, P=0.008), and postoperative 25-72 hours (OR=-0.227, 95%CI was -8.254 to -1.745, P=0.003) were independent risk factors for decreased RMSSD. Suffering from organ failure (OR=-0.199, 95%CI was -0.494 to -0.068, P=0.010) and postoperative 25-72 hours (OR=-0.011, 95%CI was -0.871 to -0.233, P<0.001) were independent risk factors for decreased logLF. Suffering from organ failure (OR=-0.192, 95%CI was -0.430 to -0.054, P=0.012), presence of one comorbidity (OR=-0.247, 95%CI was -0.515 to -0.086, P=0.006), and postoperative 25-72 hours (OR=-0.219, 95%CI was -0.697 to -0.133, P=0.004) were independent risk factors for decreased logHF. Autonomic nervous function in critically ill patients is extensively suppressed, with loss of circadian rhythm. Gender, organ failure status, number of comorbid chronic diseases, and surgical status are independent factors influencing HRV.

papers.title: Multidimensional dynamics of object representations in the human visual system.
papers.abstract: Natural image representations are distributed across many dimensions of visual cortex activity, but little is known about how the multidimensional structure of these representations evolves over time following stimulus onset. Herewe examined the temporal dynamics and latent dimensional structure of natural object representations in large-scale EEG and MEG data from male and female human participants. We also compared these datawith leading representational models derived from large-scale human similarity judgments and deep neural networks. Our findings reveal a rapid expansion of stimulus dimensionality in the brain, which peaks within 100 milliseconds and gradually decays over hundreds of milliseconds. The dynamics of these dimensionality changes tracked the decoding accuracy for both behavioral embeddings and neural network features, suggesting that dimensionality may be a general indicator of representational expressivity. Interestingly, the dimensionality of the neural representations could not be fully explained by a leading behavior-based model or deep neural network. Follow-up experiments showed that the remaining neural variance carried additional perceptually relevant information not yet explained by leading models. Together, these findings reveal previously unrecognized complexity in measurements of dynamic human brain responses to natural objects.Significance Statement When we look at an object, our brains rapidly construct a rich internal representation of what we see. Using large-scale, time-resolved brain recordings from people viewing thousands of natural images, we find that the brain rapidly expands its representational complexity within the first 100 milliseconds, sustaining this richness for hundreds of milliseconds thereafter. A leading behavioral model and a large-scale deep neural network do not fully account for this complexity - yet the unexplained brain activity is not noise: people can reliably use these residual neural patterns to judge image similarity. These findings challenge the assumption that such brain recordings are informationally limited and reveal structure in the human visual system that future models will need to explain.
